title: Heat Death
description: The likeliest end of all: endless expansion to maximum entropy. Stars burn out, protons decay, black holes evaporate, and an empty de Sitter space is left, glowing at the temperature of its own horizon. Unlocks the Entropy Horizon.

puzzle.goal: A universe that expands forever on vacuum energy approaches empty space with a cosmic horizon at distance c/H. That horizon has an entropy like a black hole's: Boltzmann's constant times its area A in Planck units, divided by four. Write the entropy of the horizon, with the area of a sphere of radius c/H written out.
puzzle.name: de Sitter horizon entropy (the maximum entropy of a universe)
puzzle.ask: That is S/k_B = πc⁵/(GħH²): the most entropy the universe can ever hold. With c in 10⁸, G in 10⁻¹¹, ħ in 10⁻³⁴ SI units and H in 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹, find S/k_B in units of 10¹²² (its horizon glows at ħH/(2πk_B) ≈ 3×10⁻³⁰ K).
puzzle.method: The entropy of any horizon is k_B·A/(4ℓ_P²) with ℓ_P² = Għ/c³. The cosmic horizon is a sphere of radius c/H.
